title: People's Republic of Angola
capsule: Angola proclaimed independence on 11 November 1975, and the Movimento Popular de Libertação de Angola (MPLA) established the People's Republic the following year after seizing Luanda with Cuban military support. A devastating civil war against UNITA (União Nacional para a Independência Total de Angola), backed intermittently by South Africa and the United States, consumed the country from 1975 until the death of UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi in February 2002; peace accords signed that April ended twenty-seven years of fighting that killed an estimated 500,000 people. The MPLA under José Eduardo dos Santos, president from 1979 to 2017, oversaw an oil-funded economic boom after peace, though wealth concentration and corruption remained severe. Dos Santos's successor João Lourenço, elected in 2017, launched anti-corruption drives while maintaining single-party dominance.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Post-independence borders follow the colonial boundaries established by Portugal, which are well-documented; the Cabinda exclave boundary is separately demarcated. Territorial extent within the attested period is administratively well-defined.
